basic_info.name: Asia-Pacific Institutional
basic_info.location: distributed (major centres: Tokyo, Yamaguchi, Seoul, Shanghai, Hong Kong, Singapore, Brisbane)

description: The canonising logic of East- and South-East-Asian institutional circuits — NTT InterCommunication Center (ICC) Tokyo, YCAM Yamaguchi, Chronus Art Center Shanghai, Nam June Paik Art Center, Sharjah Art Foundation, M+ Hong Kong, Singapore Art Museum, Queensland's Gallery of Modern Art. Related to euro-american-institutional in form (museum acquisition, commissioned installation, survey exhibition) but distinct in inheritance: it traces a lineage from Paik, Gutai, and Mono-ha into contemporary media practice, and places different weight on collective practice, site-specific environmental art, and technologies developed in-region (NHK research partnerships, Sony R&D, Olympus imaging). It reads digital art through a commons-of-technique often rooted in corporate-R&D collaboration, not the lone-studio individualism the Euro-American institutional frame privileges. Japanese audiovisual canon (Ikeda, Kurokawa, Ikegami) sits centrally here. Chinese media-art canon (Cao Fei, Lu Yang, Xu Bing-adjacent) is rapidly consolidating via Chronus and M+.
exemplars: Ryoji Ikeda (NTT ICC, YCAM commissions; canonical within this lens)
Cao Fei (M+, Chronus; often co-read with Serpentine)
teamLab (through Japanese institutional path, distinct from its Western tour reading)
Ryoichi Kurokawa (NTT ICC, YCAM; bridge practitioner)
Masao Komura / Computer Technique Group (NTT ICC retrospective; bridge)
Nam June Paik (foundational; not in first-pass graph but genealogical anchor)
blind_spots: Asia-Pacific practice that sits outside major Japanese/Chinese institutional circuits — Southeast Asia (Indonesian new media, Thai experimental), Pacific Islander practice, Korean digital art beyond the Paik-institutional axis. Informal-economy platform practice in the region that Euro-American markets don't track. Co-operative and collective practice which this lens tends to flatten into founder-attribution.
classification_logic: Apply this lens when a practitioner has been acquired, commissioned, or critically canonised by a major Asia-Pacific institutional venue, OR when the practitioner's primary working context is an Asia-Pacific research-institution-adjacent commissioning circuit (NTT ICC residencies, YCAM lab projects, Chronus exhibitions). A practitioner showing at both Tate and NTT ICC usually carries both lenses — the two readings produce non-trivially different framings of the same work.
